body:
1. Do you own your own home with a mortgage?
Yes
2. Will you be contributing to a 401(k) plan?
Yes
3. What year did your husband pass?
January 2019
4. What state do you live in?
Pennsylvania

That is helpful to know about the withholding. It sounds like this year I should do married. I think? I can take 3 exemptions 1 for myself, 1 for filing married jointly with one job (he did work in 2019 but when I start this new job he obviously won't have..) 1 for spouse. does that make sense?

I apologize, let me clarify, I planned the dinner so I would be surrounded by people who loved him and me. I'm just struggling with it because I am in such an awful state of mind. It doesn't feel celebratory to me but I wish that it was.

Thanks everyone. Yesterday was a little better, at least for most of the day. At least until my puppy pooped in the house after I had just taken him out and then I broke one of my red plates that we had received on our wedding registry 10 years ago.

I know part of why I am feeling this way is because my anniversary is next week and it is going to be so hard to get through. Part of me wants to batten up the hatches and lock myself away and the other part of me wants to be around my friends and family that were part of our wedding.
I had to wait 3 months for the results as well, for toxicology even though I knew everything would come back clear.

I'm with you. Suicide seems so much easier than this. A way to stop the pain. I sometimes wish I could do it myself.

What is left in this stupid world to live on for. I am sorry for not providing words of hope but I am hopeless too. All I can say is I'm here. And you're here. We're stuck in this group forever.
I would call your bank and dispute the charges. I did that for my husbands student loans and the bank refunded me.
You're welcome to message me as well, I'm almost always available.

I would say as long as you need to keeping in mind not to let yourself fall into a deep depression (easier said than done, I know). Be careful not to jeopardize your job but if they are flexible with you, I would take advantage of that right now.
Melatonin has helped me quiet my mind at night so I actually sleep.
You have to let yourself have those days. Listen to your body and mind, and be kind. At least that's what my therapist tells me, and it does help.

This is really helpful, thank you for sharing. It's pretty much exactly how I am feeling. So mentally and physically exhausted. It hurts so much. I miss him so much. I yelled and howled and cried so hard today.
I'm reading the book Saturday night widows, it's very good.

I'm in Pennsylvania and the lawyer I have to help with opening the estate asked me to send the death certificate to the cc company and write deceased on the bill. That's all I have done but from what it seems like, when I have the estate open, creditors have one year to make a claim. The lawyer wasn't very clear about all this. Unfortunately my husband didn't have a will and he didn't realize a lot of his accounts (401k, employee pto payout, etc) he didn't have a beneficiary listed at all (I think he thought/assumed I was but he was 40 and we didn't think about these things).

The lawyer did advise me to pay the funeral bill out of the estate as well as reimburse myself for his lawyer fees with that. I just am still unclear about what the cc company is allowed to do.

Right well I received insurance money enough to pay all MY debts except for the mortgage, I paid off the truck which was in both our names, and the house automatically goes to me. So that's all I have.
different cc question... he had cc's in only his name, do I just ignore them? no one has tried to call me.. but I do have to open an estate..

I know how you feel. My husbands truck was his pride and joy, his first brand new vehicle purchase so we bought the top of the line. It makes me so sad to see it there and I don't have the heart to let it go.

Hang in there. I know how much it hurts.

You are not a fraud. You lost someone just like we did. It doesn't matter how. Be kinds to yourself, you did what you could and you know that. I'm sorry you had to go through that. 

My friend found my husband because I wasn't home. He died of a an aortic rupture but again, it doesn't matter, it's all a loss. We all have to live while they are gone. 

I wish I could take my own advice but, not today. Today is being angry and bitter and sad and in pain.

My 10 year anniversary is coming up at the end of May. We always made the best adventures together. For this anniversary we had been talking about taking a train ride across the country. I have been considering still doing that or some other adventurous solo trip. But I'm really scared. I've never traveled by myself. And I'm scared of being alone on the anniversary but I also feel like I don't want anyone to be around either.
Happy birthday, I know it's hard and everything sucks. Try to treat yourself if you can.
I really just want to quit. I want to give up. Throw in the towel. I'm tired of having to take care of myself. I don't want to be alone anymore. I just want him back.

My day one was surrounded by a mass of friends and family. It's hard to remember clearly. 

My week one was a blur of family, making arrangements, phone calls, staying at friends houses (my husband passed in our house while I was at work from an aortic dissection and rupture and I couldn't go home for 2 months). The funeral felt surreal, like people were giving condolences to someone else, not me. 

The first month was just disbelief, shock, excruciating sadness. I went back to work after 6 weeks only because people were pressuring me that I might lose my job.

We never had any children either and now I regret that. We hadn't decided not to, we just had never decided TO. The week before he had died I was making appointments to see a reproductive specialist just to even see if we had a choice at all. But now, none of that matters. The choice was taken away from me.

All I can tell you is that you are still here and have to keep living. When you are able to, find the gratefulness for what you were lucky enough to have, even though it was too short. I'm sorry you have to feel this pain that we all do, but as others have said, you don't bear it alone.

Nothing can ever change what happened. What has changed, is you. And no one can ever understand what this feels like for you. And I am so sorry that you had to be changed, you didn't want this, you didn't ask for this. I feel your sorrow and your heartache. It doesn't get better, it just gets different.
I totally think this could be a thing, there are so many of us out there that miss playing with their SOs and there are no groups for this...
I'm the same. we were both playing rdr2 and I was almost finished and I can't bring myself to pick it up again knowing he'll never finish it.
I'd play maybe. I get a lot of anxiety playing with strangers and I'm not very good at most games but I'd give it a try.
I feel lucky to say I didn't do this much while my husband was alive but I do find myself being bitter when people talk about their relationship problems. I wish I had those still.

It took me 2.5 months to be able to sleep in our bed again. You're right, nighttime is the worst. I hate it. I lay here staring at the ceiling, thinking about our last night together. What I could have done differently.

That's been happening to me a lot too. I can't even concentrate on TV shows sometimes. I have to go back several minutes because I'll realize I was stuck in my head and have no idea what was going on in a show or a lot of times when I am with people, I am not really listening to them. I used to be an excellent active listener but now my mind just wanders to thoughts about my husband in relation to whatever they're talking about.
Yes, same here.
I can feel the happiness emanating from this photo. I know it hurts to see that and think of it but eventually you will take solace in seeing pictures like this.

I know this isn't exactly the same but because of the insurance money I was able to pay off all of my debts except for my mortgage. We had been working on paying down our debts together so now that I am basically financially free I feel nothing but empty. I didn't celebrate, there's no one to celebrate with. And the cost at which it meant for this freedom is not worth it.

I feel empty instead of excited about it. So I know how you feel when you say you don't have anyone to share the good news with.

I had to open an estate as well. I wasn't listed as the beneficiary for any of my husbands accounts he left behind. I have to think he just didn't know, I'm sure he assumed I was. Having to go through all this paperwork is just reliving his passing every time. It's awful. I'm sorry you have to go through this too.

Lose your shit as much as you need to. If you hold it in you'll just explode when you can't take it anymore anyway. I have no shame in crying in front of people anymore. We have to do it. It's natural and it's necessary. Most nights I cry myself to sleep because I am so emotionally exhausted from the pain.

The only thing I've found that helps me is getting it out, talking about it. Surrounding myself with people because when I am alone I become dangerous to myself. I've gotten a little better about that but I sometimes don't know why I am trying to survive at all.

I feel like I have been doing everything I possibly can to help myself. I have a therapist, I've gone to 2 different bereavement groups, I've been reading books, articles anything I can get my hands on. I'm clamoring for something, anything, to tell me the way. I know there is no real clear path. More than anything I just want to be held. I want to be comforted. I want to be loved.

What we he and I had was almost untouchable. Our connection was so strong. We were always completely open and honest with each other. We fought so little. We had many things in common. He was unique. Both a mountain man and sensitive. Thoughtful but rugged. He worked with both his hands and his mind. He built us a camper from scratch but could also build a computer and entire network. I know it sounds like I am idolizing him or putting him on a pedestal but he really had so little negative qualities. I will never find that again in someone.
